speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’ve sent it to family but no one has purchased a single thing. ( not saying there wrong for not) but it was insinuated they would from the beginning suggesting i make it so they have some guidance on things to get.
context: Not public with her pregnancy; made a registry at family's suggestion.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I want to except as much help as possible as i’m not in the best financial situation to splurge on all this baby stuff. I also don’t want to seem like i’m begging either.
context: Asks if posting her registry online would look like begging.

speaker: parent_unspecified
quote: I've tried chiropractic care, acupuncture, osteopathy, heat, stretching, and resting, but I'm still really struggling. I work a full-time management job, and I'm starting to wonder if I can realistically keep working like this until maternity leave.
context: 27 weeks, severe upper-back and arm pain, sleeping 2-3 hours a night.

speaker: parent_unspecified
quote: Did you have to take medical leave before your maternity leave because of the pain?
context: Full-time manager at 27 weeks.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I can barely eat, and it feels like everyone has opinions. I just saw a Instagram post about how you shouldn't eat sugary or processed foods while pregnant. Oh I'm sorry Susan that is the only joy I get with any food right now.
context: 8 weeks, exhausted, newly married.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I fell asleep at work yesterday, thankfully no one caught me, but I can't keep doing this!! I get home and most days I just lay on the floor for a few minutes because it feels good.
context: 8 weeks pregnant.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I also feel this immense guilt when my husband picks up my slack and takes care of the home or takes over the dog walking or cleans the dishes. He's been doing so much these last few weeks and I feel ashamed because I feel lazy.
context: First trimester exhaustion.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: 24 weeks pregnant and a two year old in daycare. On top of the little diarrhea pesties I'm avoiding by not eating anything from nature (but which my kid almost certainly already has) now there's lice at the daycare.
context: Worried what her toddler will bring home from daycare.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: This is my fourth pregnancy, so it’s not like it’s my first rodeo, but I really don’t remember this aspect of pregnancy.
context: UK, almost 9 weeks; too sick to enjoy her hobbies.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: It just doesn’t make sense to me because I can quite happily doom scroll all day and then I’ll try and pick up my switch to play a game and within five minutes I just think ‘oh I really can’t be bothered to play a game’. I feel like my spark has been taken away.
context: Fourth pregnancy, constant nausea.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: talking to a midwife or whatever just for them to say the sickness will pass will just make me feel worse I think..
context: After her booking appointment, where a referral was suggested.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: It’s nice to see other gamer mums as I feel like nobody gets it.
context: Reply to another gamer in her fourth pregnancy.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: But I asked my OB if second time moms typically go into labor a lot earlier than with the first and she said not necessarily. That the labor itself is faster but babies typically are born around the same time.
context: 36 weeks with her second; first was born just past 40+5.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: Idk, just the thought of going past my due date makes me want to cry because I’m already so exhausted and in pain.
context: 36 weeks, second pregnancy.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: The other I was feeling  sick and I called to ask if I could come in and get checked out to see if the baby is ok and the only thing they told me is to go to the ER where it’s so expensive.
context: Asks if she can deliver at a different hospital than her OB's.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: They don’t seem to treat patients good, or care about you. I just don’t want to go to their hospital where I might would not get the best care or treatment during delivery.
context: Unhappy with her OB practice.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I however am losing the mental capacity to go to work. I know people have it way worse and I feel bad for crying about it. […] Of course I need to make money overall though. I can’t afford not to work unfortunately.
context: 21 weeks, first pregnancy, on her feet all day at a mall cafe.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I am hoping for a quick induction / delivery and a healthy baby of course.. but honestly I think I am more frightened by how Long I’ll be without food and how much I’ll be throwing up as a result…
context: Told she may go up to 48 hours without eating during a scheduled induction.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Nothing “works” to induce labor, btw (not for me anyway). Sex, pedicures, laughing fits, exercise ball, walking, spicy food, nipple stimulation… nada.
context: First-time mother at 39+4, active all pregnancy.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Feels like every doctors appointment is me being told “we cant let you go over, or you’ll need a c section!” And then being told… actually, you probably don’t have a choice in the matter cause the hospital is full and it’s not medically necessary to induce you anyway.
context: Her induction date moved three times.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: The waiting and the constant texts from others is getting so frustrating.
context: Past 39 weeks, waiting for an induction date.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I actually paid an Etsy witch over a year ago for some guidance/tarot reading.
context: Joking with a commenter about desperate measures while overdue.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: My 2.5 year old son and I are extremely close and I’ve loved all this time I’ve had with just him and I but I am 3 months pregnant now and I can’t help but feel sad because I’m scared it’s going to ruin our bond or make him sad instead of happy.
context: Asks for success stories about a toddler adjusting to a sibling.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: But indian doctors make a huge deal about travelling. Be it bus/train/flight. They tell us to stay at one place all 9 months.
context: Staying at her mother's in south India after a family emergency; wants to fly home to her husband.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: she said there’s nothing wrong with the reports , it’s just that being at your mom’s place will be the safest than to be with husband, u can even quit your job. Make the baby your priority.
context: Her doctor's advice about flying home in the second trimester.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Indian culture sucks, they just ask you to be away from husband and stay at mom’s, when i said i wanted to be with my husband they just laughed and said he can come visit once in a while.
context: Family expectation that she stay at her parents' home through pregnancy.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Now, i really want to change my gynoc, i want kindness and reassurance.
context: After rude remarks about her weight and travel.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I feel like if my OB could take 10 minutes to review my results and my messages and call me, it would solve everything. But yet she seems too busy to even do that.
context: 9 weeks, waiting over two weeks for an abnormal test to be explained.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I feel bad that I’m worried about the opinion of others regarding naming traditions we won’t keep. I worry because there are already so many in both sides of the family we won’t get as much “celebration”.
context: After learning the baby's sex.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: It may have just been a tip of the iceberg based on already rough day based on comment made to me earlier in the day about my stomach already “showing” when I know it’s like 98% bloat.
context: A remark that day about her bump.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: The midwife says to me "you're not desperate for a wee are you because I want to get through this appointment quickly because my throat hurts and I want to get home"
context: 31 weeks, UK; third appointment in a row with a different midwife.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: There's also a student midwife in there who barely speaks to me, just about me, to the other midwife.
context: UK antenatal appointment at 31 weeks.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: This is my second child and I am far far far more anxious and scared to give birth this time around with how seemingly stretched thin antenatal care is lately.
context: UK, after a rushed midwife appointment.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I'm so glad this isn't my first pregnancy as I can't imagine how terrifying it must be for first time mums with this level of care
context: Reply in her own thread about UK antenatal care.
